title: CPAP therapy at home
what: A small machine delivers air through a mask at night under gentle pressure. This keeps the airway from collapsing during sleep, so breathing does not stop.
why: For pauses in breathing during sleep (apnea), or loud snoring with daytime sleepiness, once a sleep study has confirmed it.
duration: every night, for the whole sleep; getting used to it usually takes 1 to 4 weeks
tell_doctor: If the mask rubs, presses, or air leaks from under it
If your mouth or nose is dry, or your nose is blocked
If you still snore or feel sleepy in the day
If it is hard to get used to it and you want to quit

prepare.title: Mask
prepare.text: The mask is fitted by size. If it is uncomfortable, ask for another size or type, since there are many.

prepare.title: Getting used to it
prepare.text: In the first days, wear the mask for 20 to 30 minutes in the daytime, just sitting or reading.

prepare.title: Water
prepare.text: If the machine has a humidifier, fill it with boiled or distilled water, and check the instructions.

prepare.title: Pressure
prepare.text: Your doctor sets the pressure. Do not change it yourself.

bring: The memory card or data from the app, for your visit
A list of questions and complaints
steps: Before bed, pour water into the humidifier, if there is one
Put on the mask and tighten the straps, snug but not too tight
Lie in a comfortable position and turn on the machine
Breathe calmly through your nose if it is a nasal mask
If air blows from under the mask, adjust its position a little
In the morning, turn off the machine, take off the mask, and pour out the water
feel: The first nights feel strange: air pressure and the mask on your face
Sometimes a dry mouth or nose
After a few weeks, many people notice they sleep better
after: Use the machine every night, since skipped nights reduce the benefit
Wipe the mask every day, and wash the hose and water tank once a week
Filters and the mask are replaced following the instructions
After a while, your doctor will check the machine's data
red_flags: Ear pain, severe sinus pain, or nosebleeds: tell your doctor
Severe shortness of breath or chest pain: call emergency services

faq.a: It is better not to. Without the machine, the breathing pauses come back the same night.

faq.q: What if I take off the mask in my sleep?
faq.a: This happens at the start. Tell your doctor, since another mask or setting sometimes helps.

reminders.text: Bedtime is soon. Water in the humidifier, mask on, and turn the machine on before you lie down.
